summary: Intermittent gRPC stalls and node healthcheck flaps caused by customer firewall SYN-proxy behavior
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent gRPC stalls and frequent serving-node healthcheck flaps after recent firewall upgrade. Symptoms started after the customer enabled 'SYN proxy' / TCP connection inspection on their perimeter firewall appliance.

Impact:
- Several production model-serving pods intermittently transition to Unhealthy and are restarted by the node agent, causing short-lived inference failures for a subset (~2-5%) of requests.
- gRPC streams exhibit stalls and long tail latency (p95/p99 regressions).

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC peering to Redwood control plane).
- Firewall vendor: Palo Alto PAN-OS 11.0 (customer-provided).
- LB: internal NLB terminating TLS to serving nodes.
- Nodes behind firewall use long-lived gRPC connections with keepalive intervals configured.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Deploy a traffic generator to hammer a single route with long streaming calls for 10 minutes.
2) Observe periodic stream stalls, then node healthcheck failures on serving node from LB.
3) Reproduces more reliably when firewall has SYN-proxy and Idle Session Timeouts set to aggressive values.

Observed behavior:
- TCP handshake appears to complete from client perspective, but subsequent gRPC frames stall.
- Firewall logs show a single SYN/ACK translation and an extra SYN observed by the firewall during the stall window.
- NLB healthchecks intermittently mark backend as Unhealthy for short windows (10-60s).

Expected behavior:
- Long-lived gRPC streams remain stable behind customer's firewall, with healthchecks unaffected by TCP inspection features.

Files/Logs attached by customer:
- Sample pcap from client side (trimmed) indicating RST-like retransmissions.
- Firewall session logs showing "proxy-syn" inspection hits.
- Serving node systemd journal excerpts showing healthcheck failures and GRPC channel errors.
steps_to_reproduce: Start long-lived gRPC stream to serving node under steady load
Enable SYN-proxy on firewall to replicate customer's config
Observe NLB healthcheck flips and gRPC stalls within 5-15 minutes
logs: tcpdump: retransmission of already-acked frame seen after SYN-proxy engaged
serving-node: grpc: connection error: transport: read tcp 10.0.0.12:443: connection reset by peer
investigation_notes: 03/10 16:05 CET - Reproduced with customer's provided pcap: observed firewall inserting a proxy SYN and then dropping out-of-order segments when MSS exceeds firewall MTU clamp setting.

03/10 18:20 CET - Hypothesis: SYN-proxy is terminating the handshake and creating a proxy flow; it has different session timeout and reassembly behavior than the real backend, causing long-lived gRPC streams to be treated as idle and the LB healthchecks to see transient failures.
03/10 19:40 CET - Captured tcp_kern metrics on serving node: tcp_retransmits and tcp_slow_start_retrans_fail increased coincident with firewall proxy hits.
03/11 09:12 CET - Confirmed by disabling SYN-proxy at customer's firewall in test window: gRPC streams remained stable for 60m under same load and no healthcheck flips observed.
03/11 11:05 CET - Customer reported they enabled SYN-proxy for protection against port scans; policy requires inspection on perimeter. Need to propose mitigation that preserves security posture.
workarounds_proposed: Short-term: disable SYN-proxy or set exception for internal LB <> serving-node CIDR ranges to bypass TCP proxying
Configure firewall to preserve MSS and disable aggressive reassembly for known backend ranges
On Redwood side: shorten LB healthcheck window and enable more aggressive TCP keepalive for serving nodes as a mitigation while customer adjusts firewall (CRITICAL: requires careful rollout)
resolution: Pending - customer applied temporary exception on firewall to bypass SYN-proxy for internal NLB subnets. During test window (03/11 11:30-13:30 CET) no gRPC stalls or healthcheck flips observed. Recommended next steps: customer to deploy a scoped firewall rule to exempt Redwood LB->node CIDRs from SYN-proxy, and to increase SYN-proxy idle timeout only for those flows. Support will follow up to create a runbook entry. No code change required on Redwood at this time.
comments: Elena Martinez (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer upgraded firewall and reports tail latency and occasional model-serving restarts. Provided logs and pcap.
Rajesh Patel (SRE) 2026-03-10: Reproduced locally using similar PAN-OS syn-proxy behavior. Hypothesis: proxy creates transient half-open views that manifest as stalls to gRPC frames.
Customer (NimbleAds) 2026-03-11: Applied temporary exception for LB CIDRs; test shows stable behaviour. Asks for recommended permanent config.
Rajesh Patel (SRE) 2026-03-12: Proposed permanent steps in 'workarounds_proposed' and requested customer's firewall change window. Escalating to Solutions Engineering for runbook creation.
